claim: GRAMMAR 1 teaches that an い-adjective modifies a noun by directly preceding it, and no card in either unit explains this on its back.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1: "Modifying noun: adjective + noun. い-adj. おおきい こうえん big park / な-adj. きれいな はな pretty flower". The deck explains only the な half (kirei: "takes な when directly modifying a noun"; benri, yuumei, nigiyaka, shizuka: "becomes 〜な before a noun"). い-adjective + noun appears in ookii-uchi-ne, ks3-atarashii-pasokon and smith-bought-old-clock with no note; no card carries おおきい こうえん.
fix: Add a note to ookii-uchi-ne (or a new おおきい こうえん card) saying an い-adjective goes straight before the noun with no な, unlike きれいな はな.

claim: いいです, the affirmative cell for いい in the GRAMMAR table and in the Exercise I table the learner is told to memorise, has no card in either unit.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1 table: "いいです … よくないです *"; Exercise I: "good, nice いいです よくない です いい". Cards: ii (bare いい), yokunai-irregular and f10-apuri-yokunai (よくないです), ex10-ii-tenki-ne (いい てんき). No target in chapter-10 or chapter-10-extras is a predicate いいです; the deck's first one is in chapter-11.
fix: Add an extras sentence pairing with f10-apuri-yokunai, e.g. このアプリはいいです (This app is good).

claim: The GRAMMAR table gives 〜ではありません as the more formal な-adjective negative, and it appears in no card target, only inside one note.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1: "な -adj. きれいです きれいじゃありません きれいではありません ** … ** more formal". Deck: e-yuumei-a note "(a more formal variant is ゆうめいではありません)"; no target in either unit contains ではありません.
fix: Add one extras card with the formal negative, e.g. このはなはきれいではありません, with a note that it is the more formal form of じゃありません.

claim: The note calls まちます the plain/dictionary form, but まちます is the polite ます form; the dictionary form is まつ.
evidence: Card note: "Plain/dictionary form of まってください (please wait) — て-form (まって) + ください makes the polite request." Book, VOCABULARY: "まってください please wait / まちます wait", まちます being the same ます form as every verb taught so far (いきます, かいました, たべました).
fix: Rewrite the note to say まちます is the ます form of the verb behind まってください, without calling it plain or dictionary form.

claim: The note sends the learner to the machimasu card "for the plain dictionary form", repeating the false claim that まちます is the dictionary form.
evidence: Card note: "て-form of まちます (wait) + ください — see that card for the plain dictionary form." まちます is the polite ます form (book: "まちます wait"); the dictionary form まつ is not taught in this chapter.
fix: Change the cross-reference to "see that card for the ます form".

claim: The English begins "Yes", which belongs to the book's はい, but the target drops はい, so the answer the Production English prompts is not the card's target.
evidence: Book, NOTES 3: "はい、いただきます。 This phrase is spoken when taking something that is offered. It implies both acceptance and gratitude." Dialogue English: "Yes, please." Card: target いただきます, English "Yes, thank you. (I'll gladly accept.)"
fix: Either make the target はい、いただきます to match the book's phrase, or drop "Yes," from the English.

claim: The English "Sorry to intrude." is an apology, where the book glosses the phrase as "May I come in?" (and "Thank you." in the dialogue).
evidence: Book, VOCABULARY: "おじゃまします。 May I come in? (see NOTES 1, above)"; Speaking Practice English: "Emma: Thank you." Card english: "Sorry to intrude."
fix: Use the book's gloss, e.g. "May I come in? (said entering as a guest)", keeping the existing hint.

claim: The note points to a card titled "What a very old clock!" that does not exist, and calls ほんとうに "below", which means nothing in a shuffled deck.
evidence: Card note: "See the card \"What a very old clock!\" for とても used with an adjective. Similar to ほんとうに ('really', below)". The card meant is totemo-furui-tokei-ne, English "It's a very old clock, isn't it?"; no card in the collection has the English "What a very old clock!".
fix: Quote the real English ("It's a very old clock, isn't it?") and replace "below" with ほんとうに (hontō ni).

claim: The note points to a card titled "Yeah, it's really cold." that does not exist under that English.
evidence: Card note: "See \"Yeah, it's really cold.\" for ほんとうに used with an adjective." The card meant is hontouni-samui-ne, English "Yeah, it really is cold, isn't it?"; no card in the collection has the English the note quotes.
fix: Quote the real English, "Yeah, it really is cold, isn't it?".

claim: The extras card teaches きれい(な) a second time in the same chapter, alongside the base card kirei, so one book word has two vocabulary cards.
evidence: Book, VOCABULARY: "きれい ( な ) pretty, beautiful, clean" (one entry). Base kirei: target きれい, English "Pretty, beautiful, clean". Extras pretty: target きれいな, English "Pretty", hint "also 'clean, tidy'" (moved in by the Nihongo absorption).
fix: Exclude the extras pretty card as a duplicate of kirei, or fold its note into kirei.
